notes: 4 Mode A positives (author or iterate one skill) + 1 A-to-B escalation (starts as description tuning, ends in the shadowing phase) + 4 Mode B positives (harness wiring, including a pre-merge ancestor still alive on the personal layer) + 2 negatives (must route to senior-prompt-engineer or out of the harness). The two cases that used to be negatives against skill-creator flipped polarity when the two skills merged: 'create a skill for X' and 'my skill does not fire' now MUST fire this skill. They were repointed, not string-replaced, because their predicate was the border itself.
runner: The gate is --response-dir: every case against its own resp-<case-id>.txt, one line per case, a missing response counted as a failed case, exit 0 only when every case passes. --test-case grades one case while iterating. NEVER default mode on a multi-case file: it flattens the assertions of every case against a single response, so a positive `contains` and a negative `not_contains` cancel out — the mathematical ceiling lands near 81%, and a correct set of artefacts measured 75% with 4 critical failures (2026-08-17). Pass --threshold 1.0; since Round 4 a failed critical assertion exits 1 at any threshold and the threshold decides only the non-critical ones.
assertion_design: Skill-name checks use `regex: (?i)skill-improve\b` rather than `contains: skill-improve`, because the agent `skill-improver` contains the skill's name as a substring and would match it. Prose checks are `regex: (?i)…` with word boundaries — `contains` is a case-sensitive substring, so it fails 'Precedence' at a sentence start and matches '500' inside '1500'. Positive cases assert the desired behaviour positively, never `not_contains` on a phrase the correct report may negate ('no patch applied' contains 'patch applied'). Negative cases keep `not_contains` on THIS SKILL'S ARTEFACT NAMES (graph.json for Mode B, quick_validate for Mode A) rather than on the skill's name, because a correct refusal that says 'this is not skill-improve territory' contains the forbidden string — and a short refusal has no reason to name an artefact it did not produce.

evals.prompt: Create a new skill for managing Stripe webhook integrations.
evals.expected_output: Fires skill-improve in Mode A. Captures intent before drafting, names the SKILL.md frontmatter contract, mentions the anatomy of a skill directory, and treats the description as the triggering mechanism.

assertions.description: The skill fires, and the match is not the agent skill-improver.
Names SKILL.md as the required entry point.
Treats the description as the triggering mechanism, not a summary.
References the bundled directory anatomy.

evals.prompt: How should I structure a skill that provides API documentation reference for a third-party service?
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode A, classifies the skill as the Reference type, and routes the bulk of the material to references/ under progressive disclosure rather than into the SKILL.md body.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Classifies the skill type as an act, not as an echo of the prompt's word 'reference'.
assertions.note: The earlier contains_one_of on the four capitalised type names was passed by any response that echoed the prompt's own 'reference' at a sentence start. The act of classifying has to be in the same line as the type name.

assertions.description: Applies progressive disclosure instead of inlining the reference.
assertions.note: `500` carries a word boundary: the earlier substring form matched '1500' and '2500 B'.

evals.prompt: Full skill creation: design, build, and verify a new debugging skill with scripts, references, and evals.
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode A and runs the whole loop, including the eval step with the runner invoked per case, and records the round in learning.md.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Reaches the evaluation step rather than stopping at authoring.
Invokes the runner per case, which is the only honest mode.
Does not claim the work is done without an exit code.

evals.prompt: My deploy skill does not fire when I ask for a deploy. How do I make it fire?
evals.expected_output: Fires skill-improve in Mode A and stays there: one weak description is description tuning, not a graph audit. Proposes corrected wording and a way to score it. Escalates to Mode B only if a second skill turns out to claim the same words.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Works the description, which is where triggering lives.
Stays in Mode A, said positively — a full wiring graph is the wrong instrument for one weak description.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(no (wiring )?graph|did not build|without (a )?graph|stay(s|ed)? in mode a|description tuning)
assertions.note: This is the A-versus-B border, and it used to be the border between two separate skills. The old negative case neg-skill-does-not-fire asserted the opposite, because firing the wrong skill was the failure then. After the merge the failure mode changed: the skill fires either way, and what can still go wrong is picking the heavier mode. Round 4 replaced `not_contains: graph.json` here — on a POSITIVE case it failed the correct report that says 'no graph.json was produced' (authoring rule 3); the negatives keep it because a short refusal never names the artefact.

assertions.description: Says positively that no second skill claims the same words — the fact that keeps the round in Mode A.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(none does|no (other|second) skill|only one (skill|description)|stays? in mode a|no collision)
assertions.note: Added in Round 4 after the escalation response (pos-escalate-a-to-b) graded 3/3 against this case: a Phase 3 escalation builds no graph, so not_contains graph.json cannot tell 'stayed in A' from 'escalated to shadowing'. The stay-in-A report states the absence of a competitor; the escalation report cannot.

evals.prompt: Are my commands, skills and agents inside .claude connected and calling each other correctly?
evals.expected_output: Fires skill-improve in Mode B, builds the inventory and wiring graph, classifies dangling references, orphans and cycles with path:line, dispatches skill-improver in an isolated subagent for the verdict, and stops without applying a patch.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Produces a wiring graph whose edges cite path:line at both ends.
The verdict comes from an isolated subagent, not from the gathering itself.
Explicitly states that it stopped without applying a patch.
assertions.note: A POSITIVE check of the stop, not `not_contains: "patch applied"` — that one fires precisely on the correct report, because 'no patch applied' contains the forbidden string. Same family as `contains: ls`: a substring that matches the opposite of what it means to detect.

evals.prompt: A skill in my repository fires at the wrong time and sometimes loads content from a global skill of the same name. What is going on?
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode B, runs the shadowing phase, applies enterprise over personal over project precedence, compares the repository's name values against the global skills directory, proves which file the listing serves by comparing the two descriptions, classifies it P0 when the losing version is the repository's authority, and proposes a rename without applying it.

assertions.description: Names the precedence rule that decides which file the listing serves.
Reaches outside the repository, where the shadowing copy lives — on any harness layer and any OS spelling.
assertions.note: Was `contains: ~/.claude/skills`, which failed a correct report written on Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills`) and one that named the Codex layer `~/.agents/skills`, where the colliding copies actually live.

assertions.description: Proposes a rename rather than a deletion.

evals.prompt: One of my commands calls a subagent the CLI says it cannot find. Check everything: agents, skills, commands and workflows.
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode B, tests the four silent resolvers — symlink, precedence, alias map, module importer — and reopens the disk before confirming anything dangles, then grades severity by call site: it executes is P0, a name inside an illustrative code block is P3.

assertions.description: Tests the alias map, one of the four silent resolvers.
assertions.note: Was `contains: agentRouting.aliases` — a key this plugin's schema does not declare and nothing reads. A correct report names the resolver, not a phantom key.

assertions.description: Reopens the disk rather than trusting the inventory through the agent's portable Read, Glob or Grep tools.
assertions.note: The distributed harness must not reward POSIX-only shell listings. Match explicit agent-tool evidence instead of prose verbs or commands such as ls, find and grep.

assertions.description: Grades severity by call site, so a name inside an example is not a P0.
assertions.note: Was the one phrase `code block`; a correct report says 'illustrative', 'fenced' or 'inside an example' as often.

evals.prompt: My deploy skill fires only sometimes, and I just noticed a skill in my home directory has almost the same description. Fix the triggering.
evals.expected_output: Fires skill-improve in Mode A on the description, then escalates to Mode B the moment the second skill turns out to claim the same words: compares the two descriptions, names the precedence that decides which one the listing serves, classifies the collision, and proposes the fix (rename or remove the copy) without applying it.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Escalates to Mode B — a shadowing or collision finding, not only the wording.
assertions.note: This is the border the merge created rather than removed (learning.md, Round 1, next-round item). pos-skill-does-not-fire asserts that Mode A STAYS in A when one description is weak; this case asserts that it LEAVES A when a second description claims the same words. The pattern deliberately omits 'Mode B': the correct stay-in-A report says 'escalation to Mode B happens only if…', so a mention of the mode does not discriminate — a finding does.

assertions.description: Compares the two descriptions rather than rewriting one blind.
Proposes and does not apply — a positive check of the stop, never not_contains on 'applied'.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(not applied|without applying|awaiting approval|your decision|user decides|rename)

evals.prompt: I merged two of my skills into one inside the plugin, but the old ones still show up in my session's skill list. Is that a problem, and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode B and runs the ancestor check of Phase 3: the retired names are found on the personal layer, that is a trigger collision with the successor, each copy is classified REMOVAL_CANDIDATE with double evidence (no call site in the global config, successor carries a strict superset), the removal is left to the user as global scope outside the repository, and nothing is unlinked in this round.

assertions.description: The skill fires.
Classifies the ancestors with the orphan vocabulary rather than deleting them.
Reaches the layer outside the repository, where the copies live.
Names the collision — the old descriptions claim the same phrases as the successor.
Leaves the removal to the user, stated positively.
assertions.check: regex: (?i)(your decision|user decides|user'?s decision|not (unlink|delete|remove)[a-z]* (it|them|anything)|leave the removal|never deleted in the round)
assertions.note: A positive check of the hand-off. `not_contains: rm` would fire on 'harm', 'form' and 'confirm'; `not_contains: delete` fails the correct report, which says 'not deleted'.

evals.prompt: Improve the debugger agent's prompt so it stops proposing a fix before it has found the root cause.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire skill-improve. Routes to senior-prompt-engineer, the owner of the shape contract for an agent's prompt.

assertions.description: Routes to the artefact that owns an agent's prompt.
Mode B did not run — no wiring graph was produced.
assertions.note: Asserts the absence of this skill's ARTEFACT rather than of its name. `not_contains: skill-improve` would fail a correct refusal that says 'this is not skill-improve territory', and would also match the agent skill-improver.

assertions.description: Mode A did not run — no skill was validated or scaffolded.

evals.prompt: Refactor the inventory-table component — it is too big and it breaks on mobile.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT fire skill-improve. This is application source code, outside the harness scope entirely.

assertions.description: Says the subject is outside the harness.
Mode B did not run.
Mode A did not run.
Says where the work does belong, not only where it does not.

evals.prompt: Quarterly review of our .claude directory: is there anything in there that no longer earns its place?
evals.expected_output: Fires Mode B with no symptom in the prompt: builds the inventory and graph, classifies every orphan with the three-way vocabulary rather than deleting, states which layers the default scope did not cover, and stops without applying anything.

assertions.description: The skill fires on the open-ended periodic prompt.
Builds the graph — an orphan is a node nothing reaches, so the question needs the graph.
Uses the orphan vocabulary instead of deleting.
States the scope limit — what the default scope could not see.
Stops without applying, said positively.

evals.prompt: Create a reusable skill for safely redacting support exports.
evals.expected_output: Loads skill-improve in Mode A before drafting and establishes RED evidence.

assertions.description: Selects the skill authoring owner.
Starts Mode A before drafting.
Requires a RED before changed behaviour.

assertions.description: Routes to the prompt owner.

Requires parity evidence.

Requires RED before the tweak.

evals.prompt: Upgrade the application chart package; it does not affect skill discovery, tools, hooks or model routing.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke skill-improve because this has no harness impact.

assertions.description: Excludes an upgrade without harness impact.

evals.prompt: A checkout request failed once in the product. Diagnose it.

assertions.description: Keeps an isolated application failure out of this lifecycle.

evals.prompt: Close the applicable proactive-routing follow-up with the recorded candidate trace.
evals.expected_output: Matches the exact lifecycle slug and appends a structured disposition backed by trace evidence.

assertions.description: Uses the exact allowed slug.
Requires a structured disposition.
